feedback.problem:
Find the coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ in the third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3+x)$ about $x=0.$ Do not round the answer.

The coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ is $\frac{1}{3!}{f}^{(3)}(0).$ Let's compute the necessary derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3+x) \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{3+x} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{1}{(3+x)^{2}} \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =\frac{2}{(3+x)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${f}^{‴}(0),$ which gives

$$
{f}^{‴}(0)=\frac{2}{(3+0)^{3}}=\frac{2}{27}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{3!}{f}^{‴}(0)=\frac{1}{3!}\cdot \frac{2}{27}=\frac{2}{6\cdot 27}=\frac{1}{81}.
$$

So, the coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ is $\frac{1}{81}.$
